title: Alice's dual bit equals Bob's reversed bit
statement:
Fix a positive integer $n$, and let $\omega$ be a sample of the hard distribution on $n$ coordinates. For every coordinate $i \in \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, Alice's bit at coordinate $i$ in the dualized sample $\omega^{\ast}$ coincides with Bob's bit at the reversed coordinate $\mathrm{rev}(i) = n-1-i$ in the original sample $\omega$; that is,
\[
\mathrm{xBit}(\omega^{\ast})(i) \;=\; \mathrm{yBit}(\omega)\bigl(\mathrm{rev}(i)\bigr).
\]
replaced: Alice's bit in the dual hard sample is Bob's original bit at the reversed coordinate.
